comments: Fifth run in the leaky0125+2w+1 hardware-scheme series, and a real architecture change rather than a hyperparameter sweep: shallow_encoder=true, so down2's stride drops 2->1 and the bottleneck stays at (2,16) instead of (1,8) -- the SoC 8x64 buffer's 8:1 aspect ratio means the standard /8 architecture collapses the Doppler axis to a single row by the bottleneck, where a depthwise conv can't meaningfully mix across Doppler at all. Anisotropic (per-axis) strides aren't an option on this hardware (cfg_gen.py's stride register is a single bit, applied identically to both H and W), and the raw 8x64 buffer can't be reshaped into a more square layout either (8 and 64 are the output sizes of two separate hardware FFTs -- Doppler and Range -- not an arbitrary data layout, per CLAUDE.md's SoC section), so shallow_encoder is the only hardware-legal lever available for this. Prior history (kuralsnet_npu_seg_8x64_shallow.json): shallow_encoder alone, from scratch, got val dice 0.2887 -- *worse* than the standard /8 architecture from scratch (0.3070), so extra bottleneck resolution didn't help in isolation. The matching finetune combo (kuralsnet_npu_seg_8x64_shallow_finetune.json) was set up to test shallow_encoder + finetune-from-native together (finetuning is independently the single biggest lever found for this whole branch, 0.3070->0.3684 on the standard /8 architecture) but its result isn't recorded anywhere in this repo or in kurals_logs on this machine -- looks like it was configured but never completed. This config re-runs that combination, on top of the now-stable leaky0125+2w+1 hardware scheme (quant_freeze_iters=76000, confirmed non-collapsing across 3 prior runs) and kernel_size=3 (matches the current 0.3468 checkpoint's bottleneck kernel, appropriate for a still-thin (2,16) bottleneck). Initialized via kurals/expand_kernel3.py from the native checkpoint -- shape-compatible regardless of shallow_encoder since stride isn't a learned parameter, only bott_c/d1/d2's dw kernel size needs adapting.
